From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-08-22T09:13:00-07:00
Subject: Commit Gate Exceptions & Churn Triage — Q4 Renewal Readiness

Team —

Quick checkpoint ahead of Friday's commit lock: BrightByte landed in our "commit with exceptions" bucket after procurement requested extended payment terms and an SOC-2 evidence review. This thread is to align on the finance gating, sales commitments, and churn-risk flags so we have a clean recommendation for FinOps at 5pm PT.

Top asks (please action by EOD Thursday):
- Marissa: review the attached Q4_commit_exceptions_tracker.xlsx and confirm the contract stage and whether legal has approved the exception language. Highlight any items that would move this back to "at-risk".
- Ben: confirm the level of discount / credit offered during the last negotiation and whether a one-time concession is still available from Sales Ops. Put amounts in the tracker.
- Naomi: run a quick ARR exposure calc and add a one-line finance note in the tracker — we need impact if this deal slips or churns (12-month ARR impact + revenue timing).

Churn flag guidance (attached churn_flag_definitions.md) — we use three anchors: 1) procurement escalation requiring extended terms, 2) security evidence requests >4 weeks, 3) exec sponsor attrition. Right now BrightByte hits #1 and #2.

External note: I'll loop in BrightByte for one clarification call; they indicated procurement would share a vendor timeline.

Attachments: Q4_commit_exceptions_tracker.xlsx, churn_flag_definitions.md

Thanks —
Grace
Grace O'Connor
Manager, Customer Finance & Renewals
Redwood Inference

Grace —

Acknowledged. I'm pulling the discount ledger and the last concession we gave (Q2 credit of $24,000). If we need to offer a short-term credit to bridge approval, we can propose a one-off placement credit instead of changing the payment terms. I'll add a row in the tracker with options: (A) one-off $24k credit, (B) net-60 with 2% CAPEX fee, (C) escrow for SOC evidence.

Tentative for the sync tomorrow morning at 9:30am PT — does that work for procurement? If so, I'll invite Sales Ops.

Ben

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Tom Fletcher <tom.fletcher@brightbyte.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightbyte.com
Date: 2027-08-23T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Commit Gate Exceptions & Churn Triage — Q4 Renewal Readiness

Thanks everyone — quick recap and next steps so FinOps has a single path forward: 

1) Internal alignment (actioned):
- Marissa confirmed legal sees the exception language as "narrow" and OK to proceed pending procurement sign-off (see tracker row 12).
- Ben added the concession options; recommendation: offer placement credit (Option A) to avoid altering standard payment terms.
- Naomi added the ARR exposure: $320k ARR if renewal slips by >30 days; one-off credit preserves 95% of net ARR in the forward 12 months.

2) External ask (to BrightByte / procurement):
- If procurement can share a SOC export window (expected delivery date) by EOD Friday, we will maintain our commit recommendation to FinOps. If SOC will take >4 weeks, we will escalate to Leadership for approval of a temporary carve-out.
- Proposed sync: Friday 2027-08-25 at 09:30am PT to confirm timeline and finalize DocuSign link. Tom — please confirm procurement attendance.

3) Operational items:
- I'll update the HubSpot deal with the final recommendation and mark the deal row as "commit-with-exception" pending SOC evidence.
- Naomi / FinOps: please hold the commit in the Q4 lockboard until we get the SOC ETA.

Attachments referenced: Q4_commit_exceptions_tracker.xlsx, brightbyte_procurement_timeline.pdf

Grace O'Connor
Manager, Customer Finance & Renewals
Redwood Inference
